record.paper_title: Separability of Topological Groups: A Survey with Open Problems
record.original_question: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group that is infinite, separable, and metrizable?

evidence.quote: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a quotient group which is an infinite separable metrizable topological group?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a topological group (Hausdorff). Recall that $G$ is totally disconnected if the connected component of the identity is trivial. A quotient group of $G$ is a group of the form $G/N$, equipped with the quotient topology, where $N$ is a closed normal subgroup of $G$. Such a quotient is called separable if it contains a countable dense subset, metrizable if its topology is induced by a metric, and infinite if its underlying set is infinite.

Determine whether the following statement is true: every topological group $G$ that is not totally disconnected admits a closed normal subgroup $N \trianglelefteq G$ such that the quotient group $G/N$ is simultaneously infinite, separable, and metrizable.
artifact.status_search_result: Leiderman, Morris, and Tkachenko (arXiv:1707.09546, published in Israel J. Math. 2019) consider four versions of this Banach–Mazur–type problem for topological groups, including the question whether every non-totally disconnected topological group has an infinite metrizable separable quotient. They answer all four questions in the negative, while proving positive results for important classes such as compact groups, locally compact abelian groups, σ-compact locally compact groups, abelian pro-Lie groups, σ-compact pro-Lie groups, and pseudocompact groups.

status_evidence.title: The Separable Quotient Problem for Topological Groups
status_evidence.snippet: Does every non-totally disconnected topological group have a separable quotient group which is (i) non-trivial; (ii) infinite; (iii) metrizable; (iv) infinite metrizable? All four questions are answered here in the negative.
status_evidence.claim: The question is resolved negatively in general, with positive answers for several important classes of topological groups.

status_evidence.title: The separable quotient problem for topological groups - Israel Journal of Mathematics
status_evidence.snippet: Published version of the Leiderman–Morris–Tkachenko paper resolving the four separable quotient questions for topological groups.
